audit_findings.title: Preferred interests can demand cash, but the valuation assumes unit settlement
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.553 million computed exchange claim (1.329127 million units × $23.74); cash-settlement values are approximately $23.86 bear, $28.32 base and $31.68 bull versus $23.86, $28.16 and $31.43
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement removes the preferred exchange units from shares and deducts the Exchange Price from the equity bridge; unit settlement leaves the claim in the diluted denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The Exchange Price will be payable in common units of the Partnership or, if any holder of Series A Preferred Interests so elects, in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash election is demonstrated, so unit-only presentation is incomplete. It is not material to the stated conclusion, however: substituting the filed cash claim for the modeled units changes value by approximately $0.00, $0.16 and $0.25 per common unit across the three scenarios. The base-case buy-below price would rise only about $0.11, from $19.71 to $19.82, and remains below the $22.85 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the cash election remains enforceable and rerun explicit cash- and unit-settlement cases using the accrued Exchange Price at September 6, 2026.

audit_findings.title: Preferred economics appear counted in both the numerator and denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.720 million of 2025 accretion, equal to 3.4% of the $79.7 million anchor; a proportional rerun would increase base value by about $0.96 per unit and buy-below by about $0.67
audit_findings.mechanism: A common-only OE numerator deducts preferred accretion while the fully diluted share denominator also includes 1.329127 million preferred exchange units.
audit_findings.evidence: We recorded accretion on the preferred membership interests of $ 2.7 million, $ 2.6 million and $ 2.5 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the $2.720 million accretion and the valuation demonstrates inclusion of exchange units, but the supplied record does not provide the exact anchor reconciliation needed to prove that accretion remained deducted. If it did, the double charge is a real methodological error. Its maximum identified scale does not change the current decision: the estimated buy-below price would remain about $20.38, below the $22.85 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $79.7 million anchor line by line. If it starts from net income available to limited partners, add back preferred accretion when retaining exchange units, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter mixes earnings from sold sites with the post-sale business
audit_findings.magnitude: 107 sites sold in 2025 for $103.3 million, approximately 9.9% of the 1,080 beginning owned-or-leased site count; another 21 properties were sold through June 2026 for $15.4 million; continuing-OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor retains pre-sale operating earnings from disposed properties, while the forecast should reflect retained fuel contracts, lost rent or retail margins, taxes and the interest benefit from debt repayment.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, we sold 107 sites for $ 103.3 million in proceeds, resulting in net gains of $ 45.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, not hypothetical. Its net direction is unresolved because lost site earnings reduce OE while retained supply income and debt-related interest savings increase it. Dispositions cover a substantial portion of the operating footprint and continued through 2026, making the mismatch reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a continuing-perimeter bridge by property for all dispositions through September 6, 2026, showing removed retail and rental earnings, retained wholesale contribution, taxes, proceeds applied to debt and resulting interest savings; rerun the anchor and valuation.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may be receiving required reinvestment for free
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.207 million of filed 2025 growth capital; applying growth divided by 18.5% RONTA to the $79.7 million anchor implies approximately $12.9 million of first-year base reinvestment and $21.5 million of first-year bull reinvestment
audit_findings.mechanism: Required growth investment must reduce forecast OE; omitting it leaves growth in the cash-flow numerator without charging the capital needed to produce that growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in growth capital expenditures during 2025 compared to 2024 was primarily driven by investments in our company operated sites and included targeted material renovations as well as projects to increase food offerings.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation lists an 18.5% RONTA but its stated method does not establish that growth reinvestment was deducted. This remains an unresolved calculation issue rather than a proven omission. The possible charge equals about 16% of anchor OE in the base case and 27% in the bull case before considering later years, so it is reasonably capable of changing scenario values and the investment conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every forecast year for an explicit reinvestment deduction tied to growth and RONTA. If absent, rerun bear, base and bull with reinvestment during both the initial-growth and fade periods, and separately test whether recurring renovations and rebranding belong in sustaining capital.

audit_findings.title: UST retirement costs may disappear when accretion is added back
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.222 million filed ARO at June 30, 2026; $1.675 million of 2025 accretion and $0.092 million of 2025 settlements; net missing OE cost unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back accretion increases OE, while absent removal reserves or a bridge deduction would omit the future cash cost of closing USTs.
audit_findings.evidence: We record a liability, which is referred to as an asset retirement obligation, at fair value for the estimated cost to remove USTs used to store motor fuel at owned and leased sites at the time we incur that liability, which is generally when the UST is installed or upon acquiring the site.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and add-back mechanism are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether sustaining capital already includes expected UST removals or what portion is recoverable or attached to assets subsequently sold. As a scale reference, the recorded obligation is 3.9% of base equity value, or about $1.11 per modeled share if treated as an immediate bridge claim, but that is not necessarily the correct economic treatment. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the sustaining-capital detail, projected UST-removal schedule, site-level obligations after dispositions and enforceable reimbursement or indemnification coverage; then deduct either an annualized net reserve from OE or the unfunded present obligation in the bridge, without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The performance-award share count is not a true fixed ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: 0.311338 million modeled performance units, 0.78% of the 39.946249 million denominator; filed $3.164 million target value implies a $6.328 million maximum payout at 200%, only 0.56% of $1.125 billion base equity; additional units at an unknown conversion price are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Dollar-denominated awards convert into a variable number of units using a future VWAP, so a lower conversion price increases the diluted share count; cash settlement instead enters the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The value of the units will then be divided by the 20 -day volume-weighted average closing price of our common units as of a date shortly before the conversion date to determine the actual number of units to be issued.
audit_findings.explanation: The variable-share formula is demonstrated, so 0.311338 million is not a contractual unit ceiling. Nevertheless, the award's economic claim is capped by its maximum dollar payout. That $6.328 million cap is about $0.16 per modeled share if deducted from base equity and is too small to change the stated buy-below conclusion. The precise unit count remains price-dependent.
audit_findings.action: Replace the fixed-unit ceiling with maximum-dollar-payout cases using defensible future VWAPs, distinguish cash from unit settlement, and confirm that all outstanding performance-award vintages are included.
